Definition: {the back (as rounded); by analogy, the top or rim, a boss, a vault, arch of eye, bulwarks, etc.}
BiblicalUsage: Gab is the Aramaic word for the back, the rounded top of a thing. It appears once, in Daniel 7:6, where the leopard of the vision has four wings of a fowl upon its back. The word does the plain work of describing the beast's shape.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe even a single Aramaic word in a vision is placed there on purpose; the back of the beast carries its wings, and I hold that the smallest details of Daniel's visions are worth reading closely.
